Additionally, using smaller municipal companies can actually be better for the privacy conscious, as smaller companies are sometimes except from maintaining some of the expensive network storage and peering technologies that larger companies are forced to use. Meaning that the data they maintain on you is reduced, probably only consisting of basic meta data about the networks and sites you connect to.

In Oregon, which has been one of the most vocal and hard fighting areas when it comes to these situations, we see way more independent municipality based ISPs because they have fought and won to use existing fiber networks, in most cases they didn't have to pay to build it out themselves, they just had to complete it and run it into homes. These super fast internet towns wouldn't be so isolated and spread out if it weren't for these factors. Even Google is fighting for the right to access existing fiber networks because they have discovered that it would save them billions in infrastructure costs and allow them to expand into new communities much faster.
